Plight of HSCL 
* 142. SHRI S. RAMACHANDRA PILLAI: Will the Minister of STEEL be 
pleased to state; 
(a) whether the Prime Minister had received a memorandum signed by 57 
Members of Parliament about the plight of Hindustan Steelworks Construction 
Limited (HSCL); 
(b) if so, what are the salient points by the MPs therein; and 
(c) what steps Government have taken on each point raised in the 
memorandum? 
6 

[6 March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF STEEL (SHRI DILIP 
RAY): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) A Memorandum dated nil signed by 57 MPs was received and  
acknowledged on 16th July, 1998 by me Hon'ble Prime Minister. The main  
points raised are as below: 
Major jobs in steel plants are being off loaded to private builders  despite 
HSCL's main activities connected to steel plants from early stages .The price 
preference of 10% allowed by Government has not been adhered to. In some 
cases, HSCL has been L-I, but the jobs have been given to private builders. In 
addition, HSCL's claims have also been withheld/disputed. Thus there is 
shortage of working capital with HSCL. 
The request is to advise/intruct the concerned Ministries to settle the issues 
listed above. 
(c) HSCL was established in 1964 primarily to undertake construction of  
Modern Integrated Steel Plants. It remained a subsidiary of Steel Authority of  
India Limited (SAIL) between>9J3 and 1978. It again became an independent  
company in 1978. The Company had undertaken almost all Civil, Mechanical,  
Structural Erection Works in the Bokaro Steel Plant of SAIL. Similar works  
were undertaken by HSCL during the 4 MT modernisation of Bhilai Steel  
Plant. In addition various job orders like Raw Material H andling Complex,  
Blast Furnace and New Sintering Plant were awarded to HSCL in the  
modernisation of Durgapur Steel Plant. HSCL has been in the process of  
obtaining job orders, and of late, has diversified its activities in the non -steel 
sector like housing, power, roads and bridges and oil. Through HSCL remaiend 
L-I in a number of bids and inspite of the purchase preference of 10% permitted 
by me Government, it has not been able to get the requisite assistance from  
various central PSUs/Central Government Departments. This may have been  
because of its limited experience in some of the fields and also due to its  
accumulated losses incurred over the years and reflected in the balance sheet.  
HSCL has been getting its claims settled with various agencies. Also, SAIL and 
HSCL have resolved to settle their outstanding claims and dues through a  
process of mutual conciliation. 
Ministry of Steel has taken up with Central Government Ministries/Agencies 
in addition to various State Government' Departments/ Agencies with requests 
to award me jobs in their projects to HSCL. Government has sanctioned a 
Revival Package for HSCL in July, 1999. It is expected mat with the scuccessful

Imposition of Labour Laws by Developed Countries 
†* 145. SHRI JANESHWAR MISRA: Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND 
INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that America and other developed countries are trying 
to impose labour tews through World Trade Organisation inspite of the failure 
of Seattle talks; 
(b) if so, what strategy Government have formulated to frustrate such efforts 
of the developed countries; and  
(c) whether Government are trying to make domestic labour laws effective 
and in the interest of the labourers? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI 
MARAN): (a) Attempts were made by many developed countries, to introduce 
the linkage between trade and core labour standards in the future work 
programme of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) at the Seattle Ministerial 
Conference. However, India and other developing countries effectively opposed 
such an inclusion. No formal proposals have been made post -Seattle in WTO 
is this regard by any of the developed countries, but pressure i n future for 
inclusion of this issue in the work programme of WTO cannot be ruled out.

(b) India has been trying to garner support of other developing and like 
minded group of countries for preventing inclusion of this linkage betwee n 
Trade and Labour Standards in the future work programme of the WTO. India 
has also been taking the stand that International Labour Organisation (ILO) is 
the right forum for discussion on issues relating to Labour Standards. 
(c) International Labour Standards , espescially the ILO Core Conventions 
have greatly influenced the enactment of labour laws in India. Labour Laws 
are enforced through inspections by the Central and State Government 
machinery. The Government will continue their efforts for effective 
implementation of Labour laws to protect the interest of the labour. 
Computation of Rate of Industrial Production 
†*146  SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: 
DR. D. MASTHAN: 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to stale: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have decided to include the 
production of 543 items to determine the rate of index of industrial production; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that so far 342 items were included to determine 
the rate of the index of industrial production; and 
(d) if so, what is the reason for including these new items and the names of 
these items? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI 
MARAN): (a) to (d) The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is a monthly 
index compiled and released by Central St atistical Organisation (CSO) to 
measure changes in the volume of production in physical terms. In order to 
accurately reflect the growth rate in the industrial sector, the base period of 
the index has been changed from time to time to reflect the changing structure 
of the industrial economy. The latest revision has made the base year 1993 -94 
from the earlier base year 1980 -81. The revised indices were released on 27th 
May, 1998. 
The revision of the coverage of items and industries as. well as the technique 
of construction has changed. Consequently, 543 items have been included 
compared to 352 items in the earlier IIP (Base 1980-81).

3. All proposals relating to acquisition of shares in an existing Indian 
company in favour of a foreign/NRI/OCB investor. 
4. AH proposals falling outside notified sectoral  policy/caps or under 
sectors in which FDI is not permitted and/or whenever any investor 
chooses to make an application to the FIPB and not to avail of the 
automatic route. 
All proposals for investment in public sector units as also for EOU/ EPZ/ 
EHTP/STP units would qualify for automatic route subject to above parameters. 
(c) FDI caps in some sectors have been enhanced in consultation and with
